articles.title: India’s continuing para-sport surge - Daily Pioneer
articles.summary: India’s continuing para-sport surge Daily Pioneer
articles.content: India’s performance at the 2026 Asian Para Games was not merely another successful sporting campaign. It was further evidence of how dramatically the landscape of para-sport in the country has changed over the past decade. India finished fourth in Aichi-Nagoya with its best-ever Asian Para Games performance, winning 114 medals, including 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze. It bettered the tally of 108 medals and 27 golds from the previous edition in Hangzhou. What made the achievement even more remarkable was that India competed with only 168 athletes, compared with more than 300 at the previous edition.Para-athletics remained backbone of India’s campaign, contributing 65 medals, including 22 golds. But there was encouraging depth elsewhere as well. Para-badminton contributed 16 medals, swimming 11, table tennis seven, archery six and shooting five. The improvement in swimming was particularly noteworthy, with India rising from just one medal in Hangzhou to 11 in Nagoya. The numbers, however, tell only part of the story. India’s rise in para-sport has been largely built around three interconnected factors: awareness, participation and support.Para-sport is certainly not new to India. Murlikant Petkar won India’s first Paralympic gold medal in the 50m freestyle swimming event at Heidelberg in 1972, setting a world record in the process. It was the first time an Indian had won a gold medal in the Olympics or Paralympics. Petkar had been an accomplished boxer in the Army before suffering life-changing injuries during the 1965 India-Pakistan war. Swimming, initially taken up as part of his rehabilitation, eventually made him a Paralympic champion.Yet Petkar’s success remained an isolated achievement for decades. India won four medals at the 1984 Paralympics but then endured a 20-year wait for its next Paralympic medal. This limited success unfortunately also affected the recognition that para-sport received in India.The real transformation has taken place over approximately the last decade. At the Rio Paralympics in 2016, India sent only 19 athletes and won four medals. At Tokyo 2020, participation increased dramatically to 54 athletes and India won 19 medals. By Paris 2024, India was represented by 84 athletes and returned with a record 29 medals. In the space of just eight years, therefore, India’s Paralympic contingent grew more than fourfold while its medal tally increased more than sevenfold.The Asian Para Games tell a similar story. India won only 14 medals at the inaugural edition in 2010 and 33 in 2014. The breakthrough came in Jakarta in 2018, when India won 72 medals, including 15 golds. Hangzhou represented another major jump before Nagoya established a new benchmark. What has changed is not simply the number of medals but the place para-athletes occupy within Indian sport. Government support, initiatives such as the Khelo India Para Games and private companies taking para-athletes into their support systems have created far greater opportunities than existed in previous generations. Sustained positive results, and the stories of the athletes behind them, have also kept para-sport in the public consciousness.With the Paralympics and Asian Para Games following the Olympics and Asian Games at the same host destinations, para-sport is also increasingly becoming part of the larger sporting conversation rather than being viewed in isolation. There are, of course, important distinctions in the events and their classifications. A single discipline, for example, can have multiple events based on the nature and extent of an athlete’s disability.Today, India’s leading para-athletes are increasingly recognised simply as some of the country’s finest sportspersons. Sumit Antil is one such example. Once a wrestler before becoming a para-athlete following the loss of a leg in an accident, he has become the dominant figure in his javelin classification and won Paralympic gold at both Tokyo and Paris. Sheetal Devi, meanwhile, has become a global sporting personality through the extraordinary technique with which she competes in archery without arms, along with the huge success she has enjoyed at the world and Asian levels.There will inevitably be an inspirational dimension attached to para-sport because of the challenges many athletes have overcome merely to reach the competitive arena. But it would be unfair to view them simply through that prism. There is an enormous degree of sporting prowess required to win 114 medals at an Asian Para Games and to consistently produce gold medallists, world-record holders and international champions.The next challenge is to ensure that this momentum continues. The transformation of Indian para-sport over the past decade has already been remarkable. The 114 medals in Nagoya suggest that what was once considered exceptional is gradually becoming an expectation.The author is a sports management consultant with over a decade of experience in sports promotion and development. His work across both the private and Government sectors gives him a well-rounded view of India’s sports ecosystem; Views presented are personal.

articles.title: Ballon d'Or chaos: Official website leaks three winners in major blunder - India Today
articles.summary: Ballon d'Or chaos: Official website leaks three winners in major blunder India Today
articles.content: The Ballon d'Or ceremony was plunged into chaos before it had even begun after the award's official website mistakenly published three articles naming Harry Kane, Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal as winners.The articles appeared on the website around two and a half hours before the ceremony at The London Palladium, sparking speculation that the organisers had accidentally revealed the winner of football's most prestigious individual award.According to *Daily Mail* journalist Nathan Salt, the organisers were left shocked by the blunder and launched an investigation into how the articles had gone live. The pages were later removed, but not before screenshots began circulating on social media.THREE PLAYERS NAMED AS WINNERSEach of the three articles named a different player as the Ballon d'Or winner. The piece on Kane highlighted his goals from last season, while the article on Yamal described the Barcelona star as the youngest winner in the award's history. The third named Mbappe, praising his goalscoring record and consistency in recent years. The conflicting reports left fans wondering whether the website had published draft articles prepared ahead of the ceremony or accidentally revealed the names of the leading contenders. One article claimed Mbappe's goalscoring exploits for Real Madrid had earned him his first Ballon d'Or. Another declared that Yamal had become the youngest winner of the award, which was first presented in 1956. The articles were quickly taken down, but their brief appearance was enough to set off a wave of speculation across the football world.QUESTIONS OVER HOW THE BLUNDER HAPPENEDThe timing of the mistake raised further questions, given that voting for the 2026 Ballon d'Or closed on September 28. The organisers would have had time to prepare coverage in advance, but the publication of three separate articles naming different winners left the circumstances unclear.The incident did not confirm who had won the award, and it remained unclear whether any of the articles reflected the actual result. The organisers were reportedly investigating how the pages had been published.The Ballon d'Or winner is decided by an international jury of specialist journalists, who assess players on their individual performances, team achievements and conduct during the season.With the ceremony still to come, the website blunder had already handed the organisers an unwanted controversy on one of football's biggest nights.- Ends

articles.title: Boost for green energy projects: Maharashtra govt waives 25 pc land transfer fee - The Economic Times
articles.summary: Boost for green energy projects: Maharashtra govt waives 25 pc land transfer fee The Economic Times
articles.content: Mumbai: Maharashtra Revenue Minister Chandrashekhar Bawankule on Monday announced a complete waiver of the 25 per cent transfer fee levied when land acquired for renewable energy projects is transferred from a parent company to its subsidiary. The decision will eliminate the additional financial burden on companies, help save project costs and provide greater impetus to large investments in the green energy sector in Maharashtra, Bawankule said.The decision was taken on the directions of Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis and follows a resolution adopted at the state cabinet meeting on August 18 this year, according to a statement issued by the revenue department.Also Read | New policy in works to boost agrivoltaics in India; enhance farmers' income via energy generationUnder the Maharashtra Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act, a transfer fee equivalent to 25 per cent of the market value of land, calculated according to the ready reckoner rates, was payable to the district collector when land acquired for industrial use was transferred. Renewable energy companies often need to transfer land to separate subsidiaries to secure bank loans or attract foreign investors. Such transfers, though internal and involving no change in ownership, attracted the fee and increased project costs, potentially delaying the implementation of energy projects, the statement said.The government has stipulated that the land must be used exclusively for the development of renewable energy projects to qualify for the exemption.Also Read | M-KUSUM 2.0 may be aligned with farm schemes: Renewable energy secretary Santosh Kumar SarangiIf a company subsequently uses the land for residential, commercial or any other purpose, or sells it to a third party, the exemption will be cancelled immediately and the entire transfer fee will be recovered along with interest, it said.The move is expected to facilitate investment in solar, wind and other renewable energy projects by easing the financial burden associated with internal land transfers, said the statement.

articles.title: India's Job Crisis: The Disconnect Between Economic Growth, Education And Employment - ETV Bharat
articles.summary: India's Job Crisis: The Disconnect Between Economic Growth, Education And Employment ETV Bharat
articles.content: India s GDP growth has been robust, supported by political stability and sustained capital formation. But this impressive performance has not translated equally into employment generation, as the unemployment rate is rising. This disconnect between strong GDP growth, rising investment, and increasing unemployment needs closer examination.Historically, the data reveal that unemployment has evolved from predominantly rural and seasonal to more complex forms, reflecting changes in the structure of the Indian economy, employment patterns, technology, education and skill requirements. Thus, the unemployment problem is much more complex than what the data suggest. The National Sample Survey Office (NSSO) surveys reveal that India s unemployment rate was moderate, at around 2-3%, during the 1990s and 2000s. The unemployment rate increased to 2.3% in 2011-2012 and rose sharply to 6% in 2017-18, as per the new Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) Framework. In the following years, unemployment declined to 5.8% in 2018-19 and continued to decline, reaching 3.1% in 2025.On the other hand, the average unemployment rate among qualified youth aged 15 to 29 years was 9.9% in 2025, a 0.4 percentage point decrease from 10.3% in 2024. The unemployment rate in urban areas was 13.6%, compared to 8.3% in rural areas for the same period.However, the most critical issue is the persistently high rate of graduate unemployment, which is alarming. The official PLFS data reveal that unemployment among graduates aged 15 and above was 17.2% in 2019-20 and declined to around 13% in 2023-24. Therefore, the unemployment problem is more pronounced among qualified youth, with rates significantly above the overall average. The International Labour Organisation (ILO) estimated that around 29.1% of young graduates were unemployed in 2022. The unemployment rate among women graduates was 34.5%, compared with 26.4% among young men. Interpretation of the above-stated unemployment figures is difficult and may not be accurate. In a true sense, the reported unemployment rates do not capture underemployment or the real problem of highly qualified individuals working in low-paying jobs that do not match their skills and qualifications. As stated in the ILO-IHD India Employment Report 2024, highly educated young people accounted for more than half of unemployed non-student youth in 2022. A large young population represents a valuable demographic dividend, as it is viewed as a potential productive workforce. However, to realise its benefits, young people must have access to quality, skills-based education and vocational training that align with the changing requirements of the labour market. Therefore, converting the demographic dividend into sustained economic growth requires a combination of human capital development, industry-relevant skills, and the creation of productive and decent employment opportunities. To meet the growing demand, the higher education system has expanded significantly, with student enrolment reaching an all-time high of 4.5 crore in 2023-24, up from 3.42 crore in 2014-15. The gross enrolment ratio for ages 18 to 23 has also increased to 30% for the first time, reflecting improved access to higher education. As a result, the new challenge that emerged is converting this quantitative expansion into quality, employability and equitable opportunities by aligning education and skills with the requirements of the labour market.Thus, in recent times, India s unemployment challenge has become increasingly complex. The number of educated young people entering the labour market has been increasing over the years. The rapidly evolving labour market landscape, particularly in the wake of artificial intelligence, has further widened the gap between the skills graduates possess and those that employers increasingly demand.The Information Technology sector has been a major source of employment for young graduates. But in recent times, the IT sector itself has been under tremendous pressure. It is undergoing significant transformation, with traditional entry-level roles becoming increasingly constrained by automation, artificial intelligence and ever-changing industry requirements. Thus, there is a fundamental shift in hiring practices, moving away from legacy mass recruitment toward highly specialised, capability-led hiring. Primarily driven by the rapid adoption of artificial intelligence, cloud modernisation, and infrastructure growth.However, approximately six million tech professionals are employed in the IT sector. Despite growing fears of automation and global headwinds, the IT industry continues to be a net job creator, adding 1,35,000 new jobs in the past year. On the other hand, Global Capability Centres (GCCs) in India employ over 1.9 million professionals and are expected to increase in the coming years. At the same time, hiring is expected to shift from volume to skill mix, to pass on AI-driven productivity gains to clients.While the above-stated reasons reflect the dynamics of the labour market, unemployment and underemployment are deeply rooted in long-standing structural issues and are not new phenomena. Primarily, low household incomes, underemployment, apparent skill gaps, and a widespread casual workforce lead to low productivity across sectors of the economy. Therefore, the measured unemployment rate does not mean that the underlying employment problems have been resolved. The real challenge is to ensure that India’s growing workforce moves from unemployment or low-productivity jobs into stable, productive, and adequately remunerated employment.Thus, in India, the issue of people not having jobs is not the only problem; it runs much deeper than it appears, hidden in the employment statistics. The main issue is that India has been facing challenges in creating enough productive, well-paid, and suitable jobs for its large and increasingly educated workforce. As we witness, needy people typically move from being willingly unemployed to low-paid, informal, self-employed, or under-employed work without experiencing a proportional improvement in their economic well-being. Improving employment opportunities for qualified youth requires not only skill upgradation but also stronger alignment with the industry s evolving needs. Educational institutions should focus on imparting practical, job-relevant skills and expanding opportunities for work-based learning through industry projects and internships. Thus, educational institutions need to establish closer collaboration with industry, and industry needs to be more proactive in providing sufficient opportunities for young graduates. At the same time, creating more high-quality jobs that offer meaningful career progression, competitive wages, and opportunities for continuous learning is essential to ensure that employment opportunities match the skills and aspirations of the growing educated workforce.The fundamental reason for underemployment and rising unemployment among young graduates is that the labour market hasn’t followed the usual path of workers from agricultural jobs to industrial employment. Instead, it skipped manufacturing entirely and moved directly into office and service-related employment. This structural shift has left millions of ordinary people still engaged in casual and day labour because there aren’t sufficient factories to hire them, and they lack the high-tech skills required for modern office work. Therefore, India has been facing a unique situation in which robust economic growth does not automatically translate into increased job opportunities. This explains the disconnect between official job data and reality: widespread underemployment and economic uncertainty stemming from geopolitical tensions make the unemployment crisis feel far more acute than the numbers indicate.Gross Fixed Capital Formation is a measure of investments in productive assets, which in turn generate employment opportunities. India’s capital formation has increased significantly, reaching 34.3% of GDP in 2025-26, above the pre-pandemic average of 28.6%. This reflects a substantial expansion of productive capacity in recent years. However, increased investments in productive assets do not necessarily imply corresponding employment generation. The impact of growing investment on employment primarily depends on the sectors in which the investment is made. Unless investments in labour-intensive sectors increase, we cannot expect a proportionate increase in employment. India Skills Report 2026 recommended that reducing the graduate unemployment rate requires shifting from giving educational credentials to developing job-ready skills that match changing employer demand. Nevertheless, the report noted that overall youth employability rose to 56.35% from 54.81% in its previous edition. This improvement has been attributed to the acquisition of skills such as artificial intelligence, digital skills, gig work, freelancing, and remote work, as well as a growing culture of entrepreneurship among the youth. Therefore, it is necessary to shift from a degree-centric education system to a dynamic skill ecosystem that ensures continuous upskilling and reskilling in response to ever-changing technological advancements. The way forward lies in a stronger, closer connection among industry, academia, experiential learning, and AI-enabled education to enhance the employability of graduates. At the same time, developing human skills such as creativity, critical thinking, and adaptability is equally essential for enhancing the job fitness of young graduates.M. articles.title: How Harmanpreet Kaur rediscovered her best with pressure slowly building - India Today
articles.summary: How Harmanpreet Kaur rediscovered her best with pressure slowly building India Today
articles.content: Harmanpreet Kaur said she put in the hard yards back home to rediscover her best form, training through three batting sessions a day ahead of the Zimbabwe series. The 37-year-old focused on batting more to regain her rhythm and confidence after a prolonged lean patch, during which her run-scoring and strike rate had come under scrutiny.Her hard work paid off in the ongoing white-ball series against Zimbabwe. Harmanpreet smashed an unbeaten 91 off 41 balls in the third T20I in Raipur before following it up with a 126 off 121 deliveries in the second ODI in Vadodara on Sunday. Her century powered India to a 121-run victory and an unassailable 2-0 lead in the three-match series.Having stepped down as India's captain across formats, Harmanpreet is now focused on contributing with the bat and embracing this new phase of her career."I have practised a lot at home. The more you bat, the more confident you get. I batted in the morning, afternoon and evening -- three sessions," Harmanpreet said while speaking to teammate Deepti Sharma in a video uploaded by the BCCI.MORE FOCUS ON FITNESSHaving made her international debut in 2009, Harmanpreet is well into the second half of her career after 17 years at the highest level. While batting remains her primary focus, the veteran also places a strong emphasis on fitness to maintain her performance and longevity in the game."I am someone who requires a lot of training. Looking at my age, I like to spend a lot of time on my fitness. More than that, I batted a lot because I felt like batting was lacking a little. The time I spent at home is helping me," Harmanpreet added.HOW HARMANPREET RESCUED INDIAHarmanpreet played a pivotal role in India's recovery from 19 for 2 against Zimbabwe in the second ODI. After Smriti Mandhana and Shafali Verma fell early, she joined Pratika Rawal to rebuild the innings. The duo added 124 runs for the third wicket, with Rawal contributing a composed 61 off 67 balls and Harmanpreet anchoring the innings.After Rawal's dismissal and Tejal Hasabnis' early departure, Harmanpreet combined with Deepti Sharma to forge another crucial partnership. Their 153-run stand for the fifth wicket, a record for India Women in ODIs, powered the hosts to 328 for six. Deepti remained unbeaten on 106 off 86 balls as India secured a 121-run victory.India will look to complete a 3-0 clean sweep when the third and final ODI takes place on Wednesday, October 28, in Raipur.- Ends

articles.summary: Congress targets Modi govt over Maharashtra’s HC move against food safety rules National Herald
articles.content: Jairam Ramesh targets Modi govt over Maharashtra’s challenge to FSSAI rules Maharashtra alleges FSSAI’s parallel enforcement system encroaches on state powers State seeks to scrap disputed rules and stay restrictions on inspections of centrally licensed units The Congress on Monday criticised the Narendra Modi-led government after the Maharashtra government approached the Bombay High Court challenging several food safety regulations, with party general secretary Jairam Ramesh questioning whether chief minister Devendra Fadnavis was sending a message to the Centre. In a statement posted on X, Ramesh pointed out that the National Democratic Alliance (NDA)-ruled Maharashtra government had challenged the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI), alleging that its actions violated the Constitution by encroaching on the state's powers. “The CM of Maharashtra seems to have suddenly woken up to such an outrage that has been the hallmark of the Modi Govt,” Ramesh said. He accused chief ministers of NDA-ruled states of remaining silent when opposition-ruled states raised concerns over what they described as the Centre's interference in their powers. .FSSAI directs food businesses to maintain cold chain for perishables. Ramesh cited the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Act, 2026, and the National Co-operative Development Corporation (Amendment) Act, 2026, as recent examples of legislation that, according to him, had curtailed the powers of states. He also alleged that NDA-ruled states had not objected when the powers of state governments and panchayats under the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) were weakened through the VB-G RAM G legislation. Questioning the timing of Maharashtra's legal challenge, Ramesh asked whether Fadnavis was sending a “subtle message” to the political establishment in New Delhi. The Congress leader's remarks came days after the Maharashtra government moved the Bombay High Court against several food safety regulations, arguing that the FSSAI had created a parallel enforcement mechanism that encroached on the state's statutory authority. The petition, filed through the State Commissioner of Food Safety, contends that the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, was designed to establish a decentralised regulatory framework in which state authorities would oversee enforcement. According to the plea, the Act originally assigned enforcement responsibilities to the State Commissioner of Food Safety and designated officers. However, subsequent amendments and regulations introduced by the Centre and the FSSAI allegedly weakened this arrangement. The petition argues that these changes have progressively shifted enforcement powers away from state authorities, undermining the decentralised structure envisaged under the legislation. The Maharashtra government has also questioned the legality of the FSSAI chief executive officer's decision to create positions such as Central Food Safety Officer and Central Licensing Authority. According to the petition, these posts are not envisaged under the statutory framework of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, and their creation amounts to an unlawful exercise of authority. The state government has asked the high court to quash the amendments and regulations it considers unconstitutional. It has also sought a stay on a May 2023 order that restricted state officials from inspecting centrally licensed establishments. The court's consideration of the petition will determine how the disputed regulatory provisions and enforcement powers are addressed. The legal challenge has also triggered a political exchange, with the Congress using Maharashtra's move to question the Centre's approach to federalism and the distribution of powers between the Union and state governments. articles.title: India's sports economy hits ₹1.99 lakh crore in FY26, but gaps in funding, governance persist: KPMG - Fortune India
articles.summary: India's sports economy hits ₹1.99 lakh crore in FY26, but gaps in funding, governance persist: KPMG Fortune India
articles.content: India’s sports economy is estimated at ₹1.99 lakh crore ($21 billion) in FY26 and is expanding at an annual rate of 12-14%, according to a new report by KPMG India. However, the next phase of growth will depend on how effectively the country converts rising investments in infrastructure, professional leagues and athlete development into measurable sporting and economic outcomes. The report, Strengthening India’s Sports Ecosystem: Status Assessment and Strategic Improvement Plan, identifies gaps in governance, funding, grassroots participation, sports manufacturing and infrastructure utilisation. It argues that India needs to move beyond measuring expenditure, facilities created and programme enrolments towards tracking participation, athlete progression, institutional performance and long-term impact. Government sports allocation rises as private investment gains ground The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports has been allocated ₹4,479.88 crore for FY27, while the Centre’s sports allocation has more than doubled over the past decade, the report said. Government initiatives such as Khelo India, alongside private academies, commercial leagues and technology platforms, have widened the ecosystem. Yet cricket continues to dominate commercial activity, accounting for nearly 75-80% of the sports economy, according to the report’s overview. The Indian Premier League (IPL) has an estimated enterprise value of ₹1.97 lakh crore ($20.6 billion), demonstrating the commercial potential of professional sport. Sports sponsorship and marketing crossed $1.95 billion (₹18,525 crore) in 2024, driven predominantly by cricket. KPMG said emerging leagues in football, kabaddi, hockey, chess and women’s sports offer opportunities to diversify revenues and broaden the industry’s appeal. Funding gaps and infrastructure utilisation remain challenges Despite increasing corporate interest, investment remains concentrated in commercially attractive sports, leaving grassroots programmes, women’s sports, para-sports and community initiatives facing funding gaps. KPMG recommends creating a national pipeline of investment-ready projects, encouraging multi-year corporate social responsibility commitments and developing blended-finance models. Infrastructure presents a similar challenge. The report calls for a national registry of public, educational and private sports facilities to assess their location, condition, accessibility, pricing and utilisation. It also recommends prioritising the refurbishment and better use of existing facilities before committing resources to new construction. Sports manufacturing, technology need sharper policy focus India’s established manufacturing clusters, including Meerut and Jalandhar, could benefit from better testing facilities, quality certification, advanced materials and research and development. KPMG recommends targeted support to help smaller manufacturers improve productivity and compete in export markets. The report also calls for professionalising sports federations, strengthening athlete welfare and integrating sports science, digital systems and talent identification. Ultimately, KPMG argues that success should be measured by wider participation, transparent athlete pathways and better utilisation of facilities, alongside sport’s contribution to employment, tourism, manufacturing and economic growth.

articles.summary: All Industrial Projects in The State to Follow Green Norms: Maharashtra Min Shelar Deccan Chronicle
articles.content: Mumbai: Maharashtra Minister for Information Technology and AI Ashish Shelar on Sunday allayed concerns over tree-felling for Torrent Power's hydro-energy project in Raigad, saying any industrial project coming up in the state would follow environment-friendly practices.Reacting to Shiv Sena (UBT) MLA Aaditya Thackeray's criticism of the Torrent project, Shelar said the Opposition party leader had no moral right to speak on environmental issues, claiming that the previous Sena (UBT)-led government had failed to act against polluting companies in Mumbai. "Aaditya Thackeray has no right to speak on the environment. When he was the state environment minister, the National Green Tribunal (NGT) issued orders to shut companies in the Mankhurd-Govandi areas of Mumbai that had been fined crores of rupees, warning that they would cause pollution. Despite this, his party and government decided against taking action," Shelar told reporters. Responding to a question about Torrent Power's project, the minister said he did not know the complete details, but assured that any industry coming to Maharashtra would comply with environmental norms. "I am not fully aware of the details of the Torrent project, but I can certainly assure you that any industry coming here will follow environment-friendly practices," he said. The Saidongar-1 Pumped Storage Project, a 3,000 MW hydro-energy initiative in Karjat tehsil of Raigad, is expected to contribute to grid reliability and energy security in the state and other regions. It envisages an investment of Rs 13,505 crore. Environmental activists and Opposition parties, including Shiv Sena (UBT) and the Raj Thackeray-led MNS, have come out against the "rampant" cutting of hundreds of trees for Torrent Power's project. Aaditya Thackeray on Saturday alleged that thousands of trees were being indiscriminately felled for the project and questioned the permissions granted by the forest department. He also accused the authorities of prioritising private companies over environmental concerns and local opposition. Kailash More, leader of the Karjat Paryavaran Bachao Samiti, said the organisation's members would stage a protest if the tree felling was not stopped. According to an official, the Union Environment Ministry issued final approval on October 6 for the diversion of 233 hectares of forest land and the felling of 48,000 trees for the project. Maharashtra Minister of State for Power Meghna Bordikar on Saturday said Thackeray was creating confusion among the public by opposing the project on the basis of incomplete information. "The Union Power Ministry has approved it in view of the state's growing electricity demand, and the project received clearance only after complying with all the conditions laid down by the Union Environment and Forest Ministry," she said. Bordikar urged Thackeray to stop obstructing development works and understand the facts before criticising a project, which she said was important to meet Maharashtra's growing power requirements.

articles.title: Meet ISRO Chairman V Narayanan as he details space agency's plans for ESTIC 2026 to be held in Delhi from October 27-29 - Livemint
articles.summary: Meet ISRO Chairman V Narayanan as he details space agency's plans for ESTIC 2026 to be held in Delhi from October 27-29 Livemint
articles.content: ISRO will showcase its emerging technologies at the Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave (ESTIC) 2026 in New Delhi from October 27 to 29, Chairman Dr V Narayanan said, adding that the event will focus on integrating scientific and technological efforts to help achieve the vision of Viksit Bharat by 2047, according to All India Radio.Speaking to the media in Bengaluru, Narayanan said ISRO would present its emerging technologies at the three-day conclave, scheduled to take place in New Delhi from October 27 to 29. The event will bring together scientific institutions, government departments, researchers and industry representatives to discuss developments in key technology areas.Who is ISRO Chairman V Narayanan?Dr V Narayanan is a rocket and spacecraft propulsion specialist who took charge as ISRO Chairman, Secretary of the Department of Space and Chairman of the Space Commission on January 13, 2025. Before his appointment, he headed ISRO's Liquid Propulsion Systems Centre (LPSC), where he served as director from January 2018 to January 2025.He joined ISRO in 1984 and has worked across several areas of launch vehicle and spacecraft propulsion. He initially contributed to solid propulsion systems for sounding rockets, the Augmented Satellite Launch Vehicle (ASLV) and the Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle (PSLV) at the Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre.Narayanan completed his MTech in Cryogenic Engineering from IIT Kharagpur in 1989, securing the first rank, and earned a PhD in Aerospace Engineering from the institute in 2001. He received a silver medal from IIT Kharagpur for his academic performance.What are V Narayanan's key achievements?One of Narayanan's significant contributions has been the development of India's indigenous cryogenic propulsion technology. After the country could not acquire the technology for the GSLV Mk-II vehicle from abroad, he played a key role in developing the Cryogenic Upper Stage (CUS) domestically and making it operational.He also led the development of the C25 cryogenic stage for the GSLV Mk-III, now known as LVM3. As project director of the C25 programme, he guided the development of the propulsion stage that helped make the launch vehicle operational.His contributions extended to the Chandrayaan missions. The propulsion systems developed under his leadership supported the LVM3 missions, including Chandrayaan-3, while the throttleable propulsion system used by the Vikram lander played a role in India's successful soft landing near the lunar south pole.Narayanan also chaired the National Level Human Rated Certification Board for the Gaganyaan programme, India's human spaceflight mission. During his tenure as LPSC director, the centre delivered 226 Liquid propulsion systems and control power plants for ISRO's launch vehicles and satellites.His honours include the Gold Medal from the Astronautical Society of India, the Distinguished Alumnus Award from IIT Kharagpur, the National Design Award and the National Aeronautical Prize. He also received the APJ Abdul Kalam Award in 2023 and recognition for the Chandrayaan-3 team's achievements from the International Academy of Astronautics in 2024. ESTIC 2026 According to an official statement, ESTIC 2026 will bring together 12 scientific ministries and departments of the Union government under a coordinated, whole-of-government approach. Organised under the guidance of the Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India, the conclave will feature 12 thematic sessions covering emerging and future technologies. Why are semiconductors a key focus at ESTIC 2026? DRDO scientist and Director General (Technology Management) Anupam Sharma this month underscored the importance of semiconductors in contemporary warfare, pointing out that these components and technologies are used across almost every area of military operations, according to PTI. He also projected that the semiconductor-related business segment could expand to $200 billion by 2035. The DRDO is coordinating a dedicated session on 'Semiconductors and Next-Gen Chips', bringing together participants from the semiconductor industry, academia, domestic chip-development ecosystem and defence electronics sector. Micron India Vice-President and Managing Director Anand Ramamoorthy will deliver the keynote address. Speakers will include Bharat Semi CEO Vrinda Kapoor, Netrasemi CEO Jyothis Indirabhai and IIT Madras Director Prof Kamakoti. The session will examine semiconductor technologies, application-specific artificial intelligence system-on-chips, intelligence at the silicon edge and advances in microprocessors. A panel discussion moderated by DRDO scientist and Director General (Electronics and Communication Systems) B K Das will include representatives from DRDO, Qualcomm, Tata Semiconductor, Bharat Electronics Ltd, Anant Systems and BITS Pilani. India's ambition is to become a major global semiconductor hub by 2047, with interim milestones set for 2030 and 2035, as per a statement. A DRDO exhibition at the conclave will also display indigenous semiconductor and next-generation chip capabilities, alongside technologies developed by its laboratories for critical defence and strategic applications.

articles.content: Inflation in India: A pricey background reader center A shopkeeper counts Indian currency coins at his shop in the old quarters of Delhi on September 24, 2025. ANUSHREE FADNAVIS/REUTERS ANUSHREE FADNAVIS/REUTERS https://fl-i.thgim.com/public/incoming/rv7oca/article71612296.ece/alternates/FREE_1200/shopkeeper%20with%20coins.JPG ANUSHREE FADNAVIS Poor households bear a disproportionate burden as food and transport absorb a large share of their income INFLATION This package collects stories and interviews on the causes of inflation in the country, the forces shaping price rises, and their implications for economic policy, growth and household budgets. India’s retail inflation rose to 5.54 per cent in September 2026, with food inflation climbing to 7.74 per cent. Wholesale inflation surged to 11.39 per cent, driven partly by rising energy prices amid the US-Israel war on Iran. The country’s inflation story is inseparable from the pressures on household budgets and the choices made by governments and the Reserve Bank of India (RBI). In 2022-23, the war in Ukraine intensified global commodity shocks, adding to domestic price pressures. In subsequent years, vegetable and pulse prices repeatedly drove food inflation, complicating the RBI’s task of controlling prices through interest rates. By late 2025, a sharp fall in food prices had brought headline inflation down, offering relief after a prolonged period of elevated inflation. The latest figures underline the renewed urgency of these questions. Food prices have repeatedly surged because of erratic weather, crop losses, and supply disruptions, while global oil prices and a weakening rupee have exposed the economy’s dependence on imported energy. The burden falls most heavily on poorer households, for whom food and transport consume a substantial share of monthly income. This Frontline archive package traces the forces behind the country’s inflation problem, from the causes of rising prices and the politics of economic management to the rupee’s depreciation, industrial policy, and the country’s energy vulnerability. The articles also consider the consequences for economic growth and the credibility of official economic data. Together, they offer a historical perspective on an issue that continues to shape India’s economic choices and the everyday experience of its citizens. Read on.

जाणून घ्या, तिकीट किती आणि थांबे कोणते.सोलापूरसह राज्यातील प्रत्येक जिल्ह्यातील सरकारी कर्मचाऱ्यांची यादी संबधित जिल्हाधिकाऱ्यांकडे पाठवण्यात आल्याची माहिती खात्रीलायक सूत्रांनी दिली आहे. लाभ घेतलेल्या त्या सर्व नावांची पुन्हा पडताळणी केली जाणार आहे. ‘महाआयटी’कडून झालेल्या पडताळणीत लाभार्थी महिलांच्या कुटुंबातील व्यक्ती सरकारी नोकरदार असल्याचा संशय व्यक्त करण्यात आला आहे. या सर्वांची पडताळणी तातडीने करून अहवाल सादर करावा, असे आदेश महिला व बालविकास विभागाकडून देण्यात आले आहेत.योजनेसाठी आवश्यक पात्रता व निकषरहिवास: अर्जदार महिला ही महाराष्ट्र राज्याची मूळ रहिवासी असावी.वय मर्यादा: महिलेचे वय २१ ते ६५ वर्षे दरम्यान असावे (विवाहित, विधवा, घटस्फोटीत, परित्यक्ता आणि निराधार महिला पात्र).उत्पन्न मर्यादा: महिला अर्जदाराच्या कुटुंबाचे एकत्रित वार्षिक उत्पन्न ₹२.५० लाखांपेक्षा जास्त नसावे.बँक खाते: अर्जदार महिलेचे स्वतःच्या नावावर बँक खाते असणे अनिवार्य आहे आणि ते आधार कार्डशी जोडलेले (Aadhaar Seeded) असणे आवश्यक आहे.अपात्रतेचे निकष (कोण पात्र असणार नाही?)ज्यांच्या कुटुंबाचे एकत्रित वार्षिक उत्पन्न ₹२.५० लाखांपेक्षा जास्त आहे.ज्यांच्या कुटुंबातील कोणताही सदस्य नियमित/कंत्राटी पद्धतीने सरकारी नोकरीत कार्यरत आहे किंवा निवृत्तीवेतन (Pension) घेत आहे.ज्यांच्या कुटुंबातील सदस्य आयकर (Income Tax) भरतात.ज्यांच्या कुटुंबातील सदस्यांच्या नावावर चारचाकी वाहन (ट्रॅक्टर वगळून) नोंदणीकृत आहे.ज्या महिला इतर कोणत्याही सरकारी योजनेद्वारे दरमहा ₹१,५०० किंवा त्याहून अधिक आर्थिक लाभ घेत आहेत. .मुख्यमंत्री माझी लाडकी बहीण योजनेचे निकष ठरलेले आहेत. पण अपात्र असतानाही अनेकजण योजनेचा लाभ घेत आहेत. कुटुंबातील सदस्य सरकारी सेवेत असतानाही काही जण योजनेचा लाभ घेत असल्याचे पडताळणीत आढळलेय. त्यानुसार महिला व बालविकास विभागाच्या सचिवांनी त्या लाभार्थींची यादी पाठवली असून, आता त्यांची पडताळणी होणार आहे.- अविनाश मगर, महिला व बालविकास अधिकारी, सोलापूर.Election: पदवीधर निवडणुकीच्या तोंडावर शरद पवारांचा दणका; articles.title: Maharashtra govt revamps women and child welfare schemes | India News - Hindustan Times
articles.summary: Maharashtra govt revamps women and child welfare schemes | India News Hindustan Times
articles.content: Mumbai, The Maharashtra government has decided to revamp public services and welfare schemes run by its Women and Child Development Department to simplify procedures, reduce paperwork and minimise administrative delays.The decision follows recommendations made by the State Governance Process Re-engineering Approval Committee at its meeting on October 6, according to a government order issued on October 16.The government has decided to discontinue four schemes as part of the overhaul to avoid duplication and improve resource utilisation.As part of the wide-ranging exercise, nine scheme-related services will be removed from the Aaple Sarkar portal.The issuance of certificates to orphan children will remain the primary notified service under the Maharashtra Right to Public Services Act, 2015. This service will be shifted from offline mode to a dedicated online portal once it is developed, according to the order.The application process for the Lek Ladki Yojana, which aims to encourage the birth of girl children and support families with an annual income of up to ₹1 lakh, will be moved online through the MahaDBT portal.The Krantijyoti Savitribai Phule Bal Sangopan Yojana, which provides financial assistance of ₹2,250 to eligible children requiring alternative family care and ₹250 to non-governmental organisations, will be integrated with MahaDBT.The order calls for the use of digital platforms, including Poshan Tracker and DigiLocker, and automated identity and bank account verification to improve service delivery.It recommends updating anganwadi construction plans, issuing key result areas and standard operating procedures for Child Development Project Officers, mapping material assets through Poshan Tracker and coordinating with the Centre to track children's body mass index .Dedicated priority lines will be introduced for emergency calls to the women's helpline 181. Applications for Sakhi Nivas working women's hostels will eventually be shifted to a Common Hostel Portal.Educational assistance and examination fee waivers for orphan students pursuing professional courses will be processed directly through the departments concerned, including Tribal Development and Higher and Technical Education, the order said.The government has decided to discontinue four schemes. These include multipurpose community centres for women, grants to Zilla Parishads for Mahila Mandals, grants for Devadasi rehabilitation hostels in Kolhapur and Sangli, and provision of solar power sets to anganwadi centres.The solar power scheme has been replaced by assistance for electricity bills, said the order.The Majhi Kanya Bhagyashree scheme, replaced by the Lek Ladki Yojana, will be closed after pending claims up to March 2027 are settled.Schemes providing assistance to shelter homes under Aadhar Gruha and financial aid to orphans affected by the COVID-19 pandemic will be phased out by FY 2027-28 due to overlapping central schemes or absence of fresh applications, the order said.The Women and Child Welfare Department said the move was aimed at avoiding duplication, improving resource utilisation and taking into account demand, availability of alternative schemes, implementation status and budgetary provisions, and did not mean an across-the-board discontinuation of services.The seven schemes reviewed include multipurpose social centres for women, grants to women's groups, financial assistance for rehabilitation of children of devadasis, solar power systems for anganwadis without electricity, the Mazi Kanya Bhagyashree scheme, financial assistance to NGOs running shelter homes, and monetary aid for children affected by the COVID-19 pandemic.The department said the number of organisations availing benefits under the multipurpose social centres scheme had declined in recent years.Alternative arrangements, including women empowerment centres and Sakhi One Stop Centres in every district, provide information, guidance, counselling and links to relevant services.The grants scheme for women's groups was also reviewed as programmes for skill development, training, awareness and empowerment are being implemented through other agencies. The department clarified this did not mean such activities or awareness programmes for women would be discontinued.Regarding financial assistance for the rehabilitation of children of devadasis, the department said legal provisions to eradicate the devadasi practice had been in place since 2005. No expenditure was incurred under the scheme in the previous year, and no proposals for rehabilitation of such children had been received from district-level authorities, it said.The department noted the revised Lek Ladki scheme had replaced the Majhi Kanya Bhagyashree scheme, with eligible girls entitled to financial assistance at specified stages.On assistance to NGOs running shelter homes, the department said information available with it indicated only three such homes were operational.Eligible beneficiaries under the financial assistance scheme for children who were orphaned or rendered homeless during the pandemic have been included in the Savitribai Phule Child Care Scheme, said the order.Services and benefits would continue through existing mechanisms, including Mission Shakti, Shakti Sadan, Sakhi One Stop Centres, women empowerment centres, the Lek Ladki Yojana, the Savitribai Phule Child Care Scheme and Mission Vatsalya, it added.This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.
